sentences.text: Patagornis stood approximately 0.9 to 1 meter tall at the back and weighed between 45 and 50 kilograms.
This bird had small abdomens and wings relative to its long, lithe hindlimbs.
The skull of the most complete specimen measures 33.7 cm in length and 12 cm in width.
It possessed a tall and elongated skull similar to those of Andalgalornis and Andrewsornis.
Unlike other phorusrhacids, Patagornis nostrils were relatively tall with a high peak on the dorsal side.
The first fossils were discovered by Museo de La Plata crews in the late 1880s.
These remains were found in the Santa Cruz Formation in Santa Cruz Province, southern Argentina.
The genus was formally described by Francisco Moreno and Alcides Mercerat in 1891.
Earlier, in 1891, Florentino Ameghino named the species Tolmodus inflatus based on a premaxilla fragment.
Patagornis likely preyed on small to medium-sized mammals including the litoptern Thoatherium and the ground sloth Hapalops.
It may have competed with carnivorous sparassodont marsupials like Arctodictis and Prothylacinus for food.
The leg bone ratio suggests it was a very agile animal.
Research from 2005 estimated Patagornis had a maximum running speed of 50 km/h.
Patagornis is often considered the type genus of the subfamily Patagornithinae.
Mercerat established the family Patagornithidae in 1897 to group Patagornis and Pelecyornis based on shared features of their humeri and tarsometatarsi.
The name Patagornithidae was revalidated as the subfamily Patagornithinae in 2003 by Alvarenga and Höfling after remaining unused in scientific literature.
Alvarenga and Höfling defined the subfamily in 2003 as a clade of medium-sized birds with long, narrow mandibular symphyses and slender tarsometatarsi.
Patagornis lived during the Early to Middle Miocene epochs.
The Santa Cruz Formation, where fossils were found, dates from approximately 17.5 to 11.6 million years ago.
The initial fossils were originally thought to be from the Eocene but are now dated to the upper Middle Miocene.
The animal lived in southern Argentina during the Miocene in an environment of grasslands interspersed with forests.
Some scientists continue to use the name Tolmodus instead of Patagornis despite Patagornis marshi being the correct name under ICZN rules.
While most researchers accept Patagornis marshi as correct, a few still prefer the name Tolmodus inflatus.
A 2012 study suggested phorusrhacids could not hunt prey larger than themselves, but later studies countered this by noting extant birds can hunt significantly larger prey.
